subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme-health.com>, Priya Khatri <pkhatri@acme-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture immediate next steps. Feel free to correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Intermittent latency spikes during morning/hourly batch ingest that impact clinical workflows (~95th percentile spikes to 2–3s).
- Data isolation requirement for PHI: customer-managed VPC and tenant isolation for models and logs.
- Predictable cost and capacity for steady-state inference (peak concurrency ~120 TPS for critical endpoints).

Goals you outlined:
- Pilot a dedicated capacity deployment (reserved GPUs) to eliminate noisy neighbor effects and give predictable latency.
- Achieve an SLA target of 99.9% uptime with P95 tail latency < 250ms for single-turn text generation for the live model used in triage.
- Move from pilot -> production in ~6–8 weeks if the pilot meets latency/cost targets.

High-level recommended plan (what Redwood will propose):
- Reserved capacity: start with 4 x A100-class GPUs (dedicated pool).
- Autoscale/burst: allow 2 additional GPUs for scheduled peak windows (configurable).
- Isolation: Private deployment model with VPC peering + customer KMS for key material.
- Performance: enable prefix/KV caching + request-aware batching; we’ll propose quantization profile if model supports INT8 to reduce cost.
- SLA & runbook: SLA + automatic fallback to hosted compatible variant if dedicated pool is degraded.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Marissa (me): share the PoC usage template you can fill with concurrency, token lengths, and expected daily volume (attached). [attachment: acme-ma-poc-usage-reqs.xlsx]
- Samir / Priya: confirm peak concurrency & any multi-regional failover needs by EOD Wed 3/31.
- Rishi: schedule a technical deep-dive to validate model artifact compatibility and network topology (proposed times in a follow-up).
- Lauren: prepare a draft of the Dedicated SOW + SLA doc for review.

If this captures things, I’ll loop in our SOC/compliance team to get the initial evidence checklist started.

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa — this looks right to me. A couple quick clarifications:
- Peak concurrency: the 120 TPS I mentioned is per-region for the triage endpoint; global peak could be 180 TPS if we failover.
- Token distribution: average prompt ~120 tokens, generative reply ~80 tokens; worst-case p95 generation ~600 tokens for long summaries.
- SLA: 99.9% looks good; can you confirm whether the SLA includes tail-latency guarantees or just uptime SLA?

I attached a short doc with our compliance contact and a couple notes on retention windows.

Samir
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Health
samir@acme-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Samir — thanks for the detail, this is helpful. A few answers and follow-ups:

- SLA scope: our Dedicated SLA covers uptime and recovery objectives; we can add a latency SLO component (P95 tail latency target) into the SOW as a measurable SLO with credit tiers if not met. I’ll attach the standard SLA doc for reference. [attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf]
- Capacity sizing: we’ll size the initial pool to cover single-region steady-state of 120 TPS with headroom for burst. The autoscale config will allow 2 GPUs for scheduled peaks; if you need full global failover we can propose a multi-region replication plan as a follow-up.
- Security: we will start the evidence checklist. Our SOC engineer will need point-of-contact and ideally a sample list of required documents (you can indicate in the attached compliance PDF).

Proposed times for technical deep-dive with Rishi (30–45 minutes):
- Wed 3/31 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed 3/31 14:00–14:45 PT
- Thu 4/1 09:00–09:45 PT

Please confirm a slot that works and I’ll send a calendar invite with agenda. Also linking a draft HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-1245

Regards,
Marissa

Hi Samir / Priya — looping in a few technical details ahead of the deep-dive so we can use the call productively.

Proposed 30–45 minute agenda:
1) Quick environment overview (model artifact format, weights size, serving infra expectations)
2) Network & VPC requirements (egress, peering, IP allowlist)
3) Load profile validation (confirm QPS, token lengths, concurrency patterns)
4) Performance tuning: caching, batching, quantization options
5) Pilot success criteria & timeline (6-week pilot -> production)

Before the call it would help to have:
- The completed PoC usage template from Marissa (per-endpoint expected QPS and token sizes)
- Sample model artifact size and framework (PyTorch HF .pt or ONNX) if available
- Any IP allowlist ranges for peering/testing

I’m available Wed 3/31 10:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite for that slot unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks,
